problem: All A are B. All B are C. All C are D. Conclusion: all A are D. Does the conclusion necessarily follow from the premises? Answer Yes or No.

formalization.problem_prop: ∀ (A B C D : Fin 3 → Bool), (∀ x, A x → B x) → (∀ x, B x → C x) → (∀ x, C x → D x) → ∀ x, A x → D x

theorem final_wf : ∀ (A B C D : Fin 3 → Bool), (∀ x, A x → B x) → (∀ x, B x → C x) → (∀ x, C x → D x) → ∀ x, A x → D x := by sorry
theorem final_pos : ∀ (A B C D : Fin 3 → Bool), (∀ x, A x → B x) → (∀ x, B x → C x) → (∀ x, C x → D x) → ∀ x, A x → D x := by fv_auto
theorem final_neg : ¬ (∀ (A B C D : Fin 3 → Bool), (∀ x, A x → B x) → (∀ x, B x → C x) → (∀ x, C x → D x) → ∀ x, A x → D x) := by fv_auto
